productionReview.topic: Original intent and creator ownership before the only upload
productionReview.conclusion: The existing exclusive caller claim durably saves the exact original intent, checks live authority, and retains the original creator with its actual session generation before calling attach. The original Host reservation remains the sole dispatch owner. Neither the caller store nor any recovery route invents a mutation identity or performs a POST.

productionReview.topic: Queued original completion versus replacement owner
productionReview.conclusion: The caller awaits the complete native session operation before releasing the filesystem claim. The existing presentation lifetime revokes and drains handlers; AnyNativeWorkspaceOwner.close then awaits session.revokeAndDrain before journal.close. The serialized application transition creates a fresh session and journal owner only after that close. Each ObjectCreator caches exactly one attachment creator. The store admits either the same generation plus identical actor, or a different generation plus different actor. That pair check is a consistency guard; the real serialized transition and successful protected-journal open supply the lifecycle authority.

productionReview.topic: Read-only opaque recovery after journal close
productionReview.conclusion: The only call made on the retained retired creator is retainedRecoveryReceipt. The original Host implementation reads its private receipt memory without touching the closed journal and invokes current-lease read authorization before and after reading the acknowledgement. The replacement creator must still find the original reservation, validate the opaque identity, and perform real metadata/content verification. A token cannot create a reservation, grant write permission, select a local file, or authorize another upload.

productionReview.topic: Cancellation, account/Space isolation and late publication
productionReview.conclusion: Exact UTF8 account/Space comparisons, the durable encoded intent and active claim are checked around awaited work. A current read failure is wrapped separately so an authority error typed writeUncertain cannot be mistaken for missing ACK. The unchanged session lease checks actual engine run and account, and the presentation checks its exact mount owner and fresh read ACL. A retired claim cannot insert a late token. Any stored token remains metadata only; Host resume and the final UI read checks must still succeed before publication. Cancellation does not remove the unresolved intent or cause a replacement POST.

productionReview.topic: Known completion, durable intent and FilesV2 reconciliation
productionReview.conclusion: The process-local token/original-actor pair is consumed only after a Host verified result, whose original journal has already recorded the verified ID. The caller's durable intent remains until separate FilesV2 matching and current-presentation checks succeed. A later FilesV2 failure remains recoverable from the verified journal. Missing journal/ACK and noRecordedAttachment preserve the original pending intent; the UI does not infer non-dispatch from those failures. The best-effort live export stays inside the awaited operation and claim and rethrows the original error.

productionReview.topic: Protected storage and bounded process-local retention
productionReview.conclusion: Only original caller intent JSON is durable. The format1 record and existing filesystem protection, exclusive claim, exact removal, account/Space partition and limits remain unchanged. The new creator/token dictionaries share a 128-key bound, never evict unresolved entries and are scoped to the existing account/Space recovery owner. A recreated store has no token; process-death recovery is not claimed. The protected journal close poisons the retired owner and releases its exclusive flock. Retaining the actor can retain file descriptors until deinit; it does not retain the exclusive lock after close, and a reopened journal must acquire its own original lock.

All product changes are in PinkhaAnyUI and use the current original Any Host API. No Heart engine, SDK ABI, native engine source, package manifest/lock, project membership, workflow, runtime controller or account-generation authority changes are included. Heart behavior is unchanged and no new two-engine runtime result is asserted. The pending real transport/delegate and account-replacement qualification is not replaced by this caller source review.
